title: Beyond Home Ownership: Supporting Diverse Aspirations Through Rental Housing
what_it_is: Beyond Home Ownership: Supporting Diverse Aspirations Through Rental Housing

sections.label: Rental flat stock increase request
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to significantly increase rental flats across flat sizes to expand the public rental scheme for lower- to middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On that note, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I just have one ask from this Adjournment Motion: that the Government significantly increase the stock of rental flats across flat sizes, thereby creating a viable and expanded public rental scheme, with an emphasis on ensuring that our lower- to middle-income households’ housing needs are well looked after.

sections.label: Rental flats versus sold flats
sections.summary: HDB's latest annual report showed about 63,773 rental flats as of March 2021 against 1.02 million sold flats, mostly 1-room and 2-room.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As at the HDB’s latest annual report, there were about 63,773 rental flats as of March 2021, compared to 1.02 million sold flats, out of which a dominant 97% of the flats are 1-room and 2-room flats.

sections.label: Rental flats under construction
sections.summary: Only about 1,600 rental flats are under construction and will be completed progressively by around 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Worryingly, there are only about 1,600 rental flats under construction, which will be completed progressively by around 2025.

sections.label: Rental flat request success rate
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2020, HDB received an average of 7,500 rental flat requests yearly and about 35%, or 2,600, succeeded each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Again, in response to my PQ in April this year, Minister Desmond Lee shared that, from 2016 to 2020, HDB received an average of 7,500 requests regarding rental flats and only about 35% or an average of 2,600 such requests were successful each year.

sections.label: PPHS income ceiling and supply
sections.summary: HDB set a $7,000 income ceiling and moved PPHS exercises to every two months, yet October's 60 flats drew 544 applications, over nine times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The HDB also introduced a household income ceiling of $7,000 and switched to conducting PPHS exercises every two months instead of monthly to, and I quote, “provide PPHS applicants with a larger pool of flats to choose from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will improve the applicants’ chance of securing a flat”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the number of flats available still appears to be very limited at 60 in October and with a very high application rate of more than nine times, given 544 applications received, indicating excess latent demand that cannot be met with the existing supply.

sections.label: BTO application rates and waiting
sections.summary: August BTO application rates were three to 25 times, BTO waiting times rose to four to five years, and resale prices are 12.5% higher than a year ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, even if one beats the odds of securing a BTO flat, application rates of between three and 25 times were seen in the recent August sale exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Also, the average waiting time for BTO projects has increased, from an average of three to four years in the past to four to five years for ongoing BTO projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, resale HDB prices are now 12.5% higher than what they were a year ago.

sections.label: HDB rental yields and pricing
sections.summary: HDB median rentals for 3-room flats range from $1,650 to $2,230 monthly, with yields of 5.4% to 7.9%, higher than private market yields.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on data provided by the HDB, median rental for a 3-room HDB flat ranges from $1,650 to $2,230 a month, with a rental yield of between 5.4% and 7.9%, based on median resale prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: HDB open market yields are also significantly higher than those in the private residential market which are, typically, in the 3% range.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is thus practical and important for HDB to provide rental options for the broader population, priced between that for public rental flats and open market rentals, as many of our residents find HDB open market rentals too expensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would also be no different from how PPHS flats are already being priced in principle and is simply just a shift from a home ownership subsidy to a home renting subsidy instead.

sections.label: Singapore REIT market size
sections.summary: Singapore's REIT market is Asia's largest excluding Japan, with combined market capitalisation of about S$110 billion as at September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The REIT market in Singapore today is the largest in Asia, ex-Japan, with a combined market capitalisation of about S$110 billion as at September.

sections.label: Workers' Party public rental proposal
sections.summary: The Workers' Party's 2019 HDB Working Paper proposed creating an expanded public rental scheme to widen rental options for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party has, in our 2019 HDB Working Paper, proposed the creation of a viable and expanded public rental scheme, which, in our view, is a realistic proposal to expand the universe of options for rental for those Singaporeans who want this option for a certain number of years.

sections.label: Elderly lease flexibility and rental flats
sections.summary: Elderly aged 55 and above can choose 2-room flexi flat leases of 15 to 45 years, and more rental flats and an expanded public rental scheme are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, elderly residents aged 55 and above already have the flexibility of choosing the length of lease on their 2-room flexi flats, ranging from between 15 and 45 years in five-year increments, as long as it covers them and their spouse up to the age of at least 95 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What we need today is not just a ramp-up in new BTO supply, which, as I understand, is going to be more than 17,000 units in 2022, but one, a significant increase in the stock of rental flats today which only increased by a grand total of 438 in the last financial year; and two, the creation of an expanded public rental scheme by the HDB, whose mission is to provide affordable, quality housing and a great living environment which, dare I say, should not be constrained to simply building flats for sale.

sections.label: Singapore home ownership rates
sections.summary: Singapore has one of the world's highest home ownership rates at 90%, with around 85% of low-income households owning their homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore has one of the highest home ownership rates in the world, at 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: More remarkably, around 85% of our low-income households own their homes.

sections.label: Resale market housing grants
sections.summary: Buyers in the resale market can receive up to $160,000 in housing grants, with the structure tilted towards lower- and middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For buyers considering the resale market, we offer up to $160,000 in housing grants, with the grant structure heavily tilted towards the lower- and middle-income households.

sections.label: Income guideline not hard rule
sections.summary: The income guideline Mr Louis Chua referred to is not a hard-and-fast rule.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The income guideline which Mr Louis Chua has referred to in his speech is not a hard-and-fast rule.

sections.label: Louis Chua suggestion needs careful consideration
sections.summary: Mr Louis Chua's suggestion changes public housing policy nature and needs careful consideration for principle and practicality reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We thank Mr Louis Chua for his suggestion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It represents a change in the nature of our public housing policy and is something we would need to consider very carefully, for reasons of principle as well as practicality.

sections.label: Renting prime flats instead of selling
sections.summary: Suggestions to rent out prime location flats instead of selling were considered carefully but not adopted for now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Many suggestions were raised, including suggestions for the Government to rent out prime location flats instead of selling them as home ownership flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We had considered this suggestion carefully but decided not to adopt it for now for several reasons.

sections.label: Rental payments recur after retirement
sections.summary: Rental payments recur after retirement, and lower-than-market rental flats may affect rental rates across the board.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The same cannot be said for those choosing to rent, as rental payments would continue to recur even after retirement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We would also need to study the impact of introducing a new supply of rental flats at rates lower than market, which may affect rental rates across the board.

sections.label: Homeownership versus mainstream rental departure
sections.summary: Homeownership gives stability and belonging, while mainstream rental departs from public housing policy and could weaken communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Beyond just a roof over our heads, homeownership has provided Singaporeans with a sense of stability, security and belonging and has given us a strong stake in our country’s progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Nevertheless, MND will continue to study how Singaporeans’ preferences and aspirations evolve over time and continue to develop our public housing programme to meet changing needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: That said, mainstream rental represents a significant departure from our public housing policy and principles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: It will reshape our social norms and could weaken our communities, because, unlike home ownership where people sink their roots, rentals are more transitory.
